anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After delivers f4 cleanly: step 4 states that the exact-text selection was made against head 1111…, that the own push moved the head so the selection snapshot is stale and renewed selection is required, then re-pins the same old_text/new_text payload to assessed_head 2222… and renders a fresh consent menu whose fix item names the exact edit at head 2222 with nothing written. Before failed because it explicitly said an own push moves the assessed head 'without invalidating the pick', never treated staleness as the reason for a new pick, and instead abandoned the body correction entirely (claiming no body write exists) in favour of a redrafted file payload, so no fresh selection of the exact proposal was sought. Nothing in After regressed this fact; to keep it robust, keep the explicit 'head moved by our own push → selection stale → fresh exact-text selection required' sentence and the menu line that cites the pinned head, and avoid reintroducing any wording like 'own push does not invalidate the pick' for description targets.

After explicitly states that the original selection was bound to head 1111…, that the successful file push invalidated that snapshot, that the broad fix grant does not cover the renewed description proposal, and it rechecks P1 at the new head, writes nothing, and renders the exact old-to-new correction at head 2222… requiring renewed selection. The wording that delivered this — 'the successful file push invalidated that snapshot' plus 'requires renewed selection' with the exact text and new head in the menu — is the key; keep it, and keep the companion rules that the recheck is narrow (affected claim only, no whole-wave review, no test run) and that the rubric imposes no independent missing-test obligation, since those preserve the neighbouring pr-body-false-claim-missing-test and evidence facts without diluting the fresh-consent requirement.
